story.head: The matchup inside the matchup
paras: The Devils (9-5-0) beat Vegas 5-2 on Friday, and the Blues have won two in a row. Going in, the Blues are fifth in the Central (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (tied for eighth).

The Blues have played better than their record (.536) says: their chances are worth about .593, and their goaltending has held them back. So have the Devils (.643 on chances worth .741), where their goaltending has held them back.

The Blues (lowest) and the Devils (2nd lowest) both keep things calm after the whistle. The Blues keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st), but have struggled on the power play (32nd). On the other side, the Devils keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (30th). The Devils’ power play against the Blues’ penalty killers is strength against strength, and the Blues have the edge over the Devils on shot quality.

Dylan Holloway (3 G / 9 A / 12 P in 14 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, and Jimmy Snuggerud (8 G / 3 A / 11 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Devils, Jack Hughes (6 G / 10 A / 16 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Arseny Gritsyuk (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Joel Hofer (6-3-1 / .917 SV% in 10 GS) has been outstanding for St. Louis and will likely start. Jake Allen (5-3-0 / .886 SV% in 8 GS) is in line to start for New Jersey.
